body.p: A ready-to-use implementation is available via the Oxygen AI Positron Hooks add-on. It implements this extension point and dispatches hook events to external scripts configured in a JSON file, without requiring any Java code.

strow.stentry: Fired before an inline autocomplete suggestion is requested. Veto to suppress the suggestion.
Fired after an inline autocomplete suggestion has been generated.

dlentry.dd: Fired before an inline autocomplete suggestion is requested from the AI model. Throwing an exception suppresses the suggestion — no AI call is made and no ghost text is shown.

strow.stentry: URL of the document open in the editor at the time the suggestion was triggered.
The text context used as input for the suggestion.

dlentry.dd: Fired after an inline autocomplete suggestion has been generated by the AI model. Use it for auditing, token-usage tracking, or analytics on autocomplete activity. Note that this event fires regardless of whether the user accepts or dismisses the ghost text.

strow.stentry: URL of the document for which the suggestion was generated.
The autocomplete suggestion text generated by the AI model. Absent when no suggestion was produced.
Token usage for this completion request. Contains prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, and total_tokens. Absent when not reported by the backend.

body.p:
Tools called through the Oxygen MCP server - The tools that third-party AI assistants (such as Claude Code or GitHub Copilot) call through the Oxygen MCP server trigger the same hook events as the tools called in the AI chat:
preToolUse, followed by postToolUse or postToolUseFailure, and the events that the tool fires itself, such as beforeEditFile, beforeReadFile, beforeLoadSkill, or subagentStart. When a handler vetoes a blocking event, the tool (or, for an event that the tool fires itself, the vetoed operation) does not run, and the AI assistant receives an error that contains the veto message.
The events of the AI actions and sub-agents that such a tool starts (for example, through the invoke_ai_agent tool), including their own tool calls. All these events report mcp_server in their invocation_source field. For a tool that the AI assistant calls directly, there is no AI Positron chat session: the session_id field holds the identifier of the MCP session of the assistant, which a sub-agent started by the tool reports as its parent_session_id, and no prompt or response events are fired. The MCP session itself is reported as a session of type mcp_server and sessionStart is fired when the AI assistant connects to the server and sessionEnd when its session ends, with one of the following reasons:
client_close - The AI assistant ended its session.
connection_lost - The AI assistant could no longer be reached (for example, because it dropped its connection while waiting for the result of a tool). An assistant usually starts a new session then, so one connection of an assistant can be reported as several sessions.
server_stop - The Oxygen MCP server was stopped from its preferences page.
application_close - was closed. There is no idle timeout: an AI assistant that disconnects without ending its session, while no tool result or notification is being sent to it, is reported as ended only when the server stops or closes. The payloads of all these events also name the MCP client of the AI assistant, as it introduced itself when it connected to the server:
Field Type Description
mcp_client_name string Name of the MCP client (e.g. claude-code). Omitted when the client gave none.
mcp_client_version string Version of the MCP client. Omitted when the client gave none.

dlentry.dd: It is also fired when an AI assistant connects to the Oxygen MCP server, with mcp_server as its session_type (see Tools called through the Oxygen MCP server in the overview above).

It is also fired when the session of an AI assistant connected to the Oxygen MCP server ends, with mcp_server as its session_type and client_close, connection_lost, server_stop, or application_close as its reason (see Tools called through the Oxygen MCP server in the overview above).

strow.stentry: The route through which the run that fired the event was started from outside AI Positron: mcp_server for a tool called through the Oxygen MCP server, and for the AI actions and sub-agents that such a tool starts. Omitted when AI Positron started the run itself.
